::: {.why}
An unweighted fit chases the far wings where quotes are wide and nobody trades, and choosing the weight is the difference between a fit that describes the market and one that describes its noise.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Fit SVI slice by slice with a defensible weighting and report the fit quality in volatility points and in price.
- Check the fitted surface against all three no-arbitrage conditions, including across maturities.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Fit each maturity with the admissibility constraint enforced during optimisation rather than checked afterwards, weighting by vega or by the reciprocal of the spread so the fit concentrates where quotes are meaningful. Report residuals in implied volatility points and in price, since a large volatility error on a deep wing can be a tiny price error.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Check calendar arbitrage across the fitted slices, which is the condition that slice-by-slice fitting can violate even when each slice is individually fine. Where it fails, note it rather than patching it, and record which maturity pairs are involved.
:::
:::

## Checkpoint

Your fit has a 2 volatility point error on a deep out-of-the-money put. Is that a problem? Answer in price terms.
:::
